sentences.text:
Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:166682
Court No. - 70

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 36141 of 2023
Applicant :- Dinesh

Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Rajendra Prasad
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.

1. Heard Sri Vinod Singh Advocate holding brief of Rajendra Prasad, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Pradeep Kumar, learned AGA for the State-respondent.
2.

The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
206 of 2023, under Sections 498A, 323, 506 & 376 IPC and Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Bilari, District Moradabad, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged on 24.5.2023 against the applicant, his brother Dinesh and his wife Mamta and according to the FIR, marriage of the younger brother of the applicant was performed with the informant and thereafter applicant alongwith his younger brother and his wife tortured the informant for dowry and on 17.4.2023, he committed rape with her.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless and applicant is jeth of the informant and as some matrimonial dispute was pending between the applicant and prosecutrix, therefore, on the basis of wild allegation of Dinesh vs State Of U.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106185056/
1 rape, applicant has been made accused in the present matter.
5.

He further submitted that as per the prosecutrix rape was committed by the applicant on 17.4.2023 but FIR was lodged on 24.5.2023 i.e after more than a month and this fact clearly suggests that the allegation of rape made against the applicant is false.

6. He further submitted that on 17.4.2023 i.e. on the date of alleged rape, a NCR was lodged by the husband of the informant against the informant and her family members under section 323 IPC which has been annexed as annexure-5 to the affidavit filed in support of the instant bail application and this fact again shows that the relationship of the prosecutrix was not cordial with the family members of her husband and the present case is the outcome of the matrimonial dispute arose between both the sides.
7.

He further submitted that even from perusal of the FIR of the present case, it appears that entire allegation of rape made against the applicant is totally false and baseless and no reliance can be placed on such version.
8.
He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 7.6.2023, therefore, he may be released on bail.
9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the arguments on fact advanced by learned counsel for the applicant.
10. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. Although, prosecutrix i.e. informant of the case in the FIR as well as in both the statements recorded under sections 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. made allegation of rape against the applicant but admittedly, applicant is her Jeth and matrimonial dispute is pending between both the sides.

12.Further, as per allegation, rape was committed by the applicant on 17.4.2023 but FIR of the alleged incident of rape was lodged on 24.5.2023 i.e. after more than a month.
13.

Further, from annexure-5 it reflects that on 17.4.2023 i.e. on the date of alleged rape, a NCR was lodged by the younger brother of the applicant i.e. husband of the informant against the informant and her family members and this fact again strengthen the fact that some dispute was pending between both the sides.

14. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, in my view,
applicant is entitled to be released on bail.
15. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant bail application is allowed.

Dinesh vs State Of U.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106185056/
2 16.

Let the applicant-Dinesh, be released on bail in the aforesaid case on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall appear before the trial court on the dates fixed, unless his personal presence is exempted.

(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the Court or any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) The applicant shall not indulge in any criminal and anti-social activity.
17. In case of breach of any of the above condition, the prosecution will be at liberty to move an application before this Court for cancellation of the bail of the applicant.

18. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 18.8.2023 Ankita  Dinesh vs State Of U.P. on 18 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/106185056/
